T0800.name: Activate Firmware Update Mode
T0800.description: Adversaries may activate firmware update mode on ICS devices to prevent normal operation. This technique targets PLCs, RTUs, and intelligent electronic devices (IEDs) in substations and distribution automation systems.
mitigations: Access Management: Restrict firmware update capabilities to authorized engineering workstations.
Network Segmentation: Isolate firmware update networks from operational networks.
Communication Authenticity: Validate firmware images with cryptographic signatures.

T0855.name: Unauthorized Command Message
T0855.description: Adversaries may send unauthorized command messages to ICS controllers to manipulate physical processes. Targets Modbus, DNP3, IEC 61850, and IEC 104 protocols used in power grid SCADA systems.
mitigations: Network Allowlisting: Only allow commands from authorized sources.
Communication Authenticity: Implement secure authentication on industrial protocols.
Monitoring: Deploy passive IDS to monitor for anomalous control commands.
Network Segmentation: Separate control networks from corporate IT.

T0831.name: Manipulation of Control
T0831.description: Adversaries may manipulate control logic or control systems to cause physical damage or disruption. In smart grids, this can lead to voltage instability, load shedding, or transformer damage.
mitigations: Safety Instrumented Systems: Deploy independent safety systems.
Network Segmentation: Isolate safety-critical control loops.
Monitoring: Implement process anomaly detection.
Data Backup: Maintain golden copies of control logic.

T0826.name: Loss of Availability
T0826.description: Adversaries may cause loss of availability of ICS functions and services. In power grids, this disrupts SCADA visibility, metering, and automated protective relaying.
mitigations: Redundancy: Deploy redundant communication paths and servers.
Data Backup: Maintain regular backups of historian and configuration data.
Network Segmentation: Prevent lateral movement between IT and OT.
Emergency Operation Procedures: Train operators for manual fallback.

T0814.name: Denial of Service
T0814.description: Adversaries may perform denial of service attacks to disrupt ICS operations. Flooding Modbus or DNP3 endpoints can cause RTUs or PLCs to become unresponsive.
mitigations: Network Intrusion Prevention: Deploy IDS/IPS tuned for ICS protocols.
Filter Network Traffic: Rate-limit traffic to ICS endpoints.
Redundancy: Ensure backup communication channels.

T0886.name: Remote Services
T0886.description: Adversaries may leverage remote services (RDP, SSH, VNC, or vendor-specific tools) to gain access to ICS networks. Jump hosts and engineering workstations are primary targets.
mitigations: Multi-Factor Authentication: Require MFA for all remote access.
Network Segmentation: Use demilitarized zones (DMZ) between IT and OT.
Account Management: Regularly audit remote access accounts.
